authority: District Magistrate / Revenue Department (State level); National Commission for Backward Classes (Central level)

description.en: OBC Certificate is issued to members of communities listed in the Central or State List of Other Backward Classes. The certificate is required for availing reservation benefits in central and state government jobs, educational institutions, and various welfare schemes.

verifiedConditions.claim: The applicant's community must be listed in the Central List of Other Backward Classes maintained by the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) or in the respective State List of OBCs.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: Applicants seeking OBC Non-Creamy Layer certificate for central government benefits
verifiedConditions.claim: For availing reservation benefits in central government services and educational institutions, the applicant's family income must be below the creamy layer threshold (currently Rs. 8 lakhs per annum) as defined by the Department of Personnel and Training.

unverifiedEligibility: State-level OBC lists may differ from the central list. Some communities may be listed in one but not the other.
Creamy layer income threshold may be revised periodically by the government.
Children of OBC parents who are government employees above a certain grade may fall in the creamy layer.
Some states issue separate OBC certificates for state and central purposes.

requirements.claim: Prescribed application form available at the district/tehsil office or downloadable from the state's e-district portal.
Aadhaar card of the applicant for identity verification and address proof.
Proof of caste/community — either father's OBC certificate, community verification report from the local authority (Gram Pradhan, Sarpanch, or Ward Member), or an affidavit on stamp paper.

Self-declaration of family income or income certificate from the competent authority for determining creamy layer/non-creamy layer status. Family income is computed for the three preceding financial years.
Proof of residence in the state/district where the certificate is being applied for — ration card, voter ID, domicile certificate, or utility bills.
Recent passport-size photographs of the applicant.

processInformation.claim: Apply through the state's e-district portal or visit the district/tehsil/SDM office with required documents. In many states, applications can also be submitted through Common Service Centres (CSCs) or Lok Seva Kendras.

Submitted documents are verified by the revenue department. A field verification or inquiry may be conducted through the local Lekhpal/Patwari or revenue inspector to verify the applicant's caste and residence.
The application is processed and approved by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) or Tehsildar or other competent authority designated by the state government.

The OBC certificate is generated digitally or physically and can be downloaded from the e-district portal or collected from the issuing office. The certificate typically includes the applicant's name, father's name, caste/community, and creamy layer/non-creamy layer status.

output.claim: An OBC Certificate is issued containing the applicant's personal details, caste/community name, whether the community is listed in the Central or State OBC list, and non-creamy layer declaration (if applicable). The certificate is valid for use in government job applications, educational admissions, and welfare scheme enrollment.

fees.claim: Application fee ranges from Rs. 10 to Rs. 50 depending on the state. Some states do not charge any fee for OBC certificate issuance. Online applications may have an additional nominal service charge.

processingTime.applicability: OBC certificate from application to issuance
processingTime.claim: OBC certificate processing typically takes 15-30 days depending on the state, district workload, and whether field verification is required. Some states have implemented time-bound service delivery guarantees under their Public Service Guarantee Acts.

sources.title: National Commission for Backward Classes — Official Portal
sources.publisher: National Commission for Backward Classes, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The NCBC portal provides the Central List of Other Backward Classes, state-wise community listings, and information on the statutory functions of the Commission. The portal also lists the criteria for inclusion in the OBC list.
claimsSupported: Central List of OBC communities is maintained by NCBC.
Communities must be listed in the Central or State list to be eligible for OBC certificate.
Creamy layer/non-creamy layer distinction applies for central government benefits.
sources.uncertainty: The central and state OBC lists are updated periodically. Some communities may be added or removed through government notifications.

sources.title: Department of Personnel and Training — OBC Creamy Layer Criteria
sources.publisher: Department of Personnel and Training, Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: DoPT office memoranda define the creamy layer criteria for OBC reservation. The current income threshold for non-creamy layer status is Rs. 8 lakhs per annum gross annual income of the parents.
claimsSupported: Creamy layer income threshold is Rs. 8 lakhs per annum.
Family income is computed for three preceding financial years.
Children of Group A/B government officers are in creamy layer regardless of income.
sources.uncertainty: The creamy layer threshold may be revised. The criteria have been updated multiple times since inception.

sources.title: e-District Portal (representative state portal for OBC certificate)
sources.publisher: Revenue Department, State Government (example: Uttar Pradesh)
sources.evidenceExcerpt: State e-district portals provide the online application facility for OBC certificate along with document requirements, fee information, and processing timelines. The application process is similar across most states though specific documents and fees may vary.
claimsSupported: Application can be submitted online through e-district portals.
Required documents include identity proof, caste proof, income declaration, and address proof.
Fee ranges from Rs. 10 to Rs. 50.
sources.uncertainty: This source represents one state's implementation. Other states have their own portals with varying processes, fees, and timelines.

limitations: This record provides a general overview applicable across states. Specific documentation requirements, fees, and processing timelines vary significantly by state.
The record uses one state's e-district portal as representative. Applicants must check their specific state's portal.
The record does not cover the process for new community inclusion in the OBC list.
Creamy layer criteria and income thresholds are subject to periodic revision.
The record does not cover OBC certificate validation or renewal processes in detail.
State-specific variations in field verification procedures are not modeled.

review.reviewReason: Central eligibility criteria are reviewed, but state-specific implementation details need verification across all major states.
nextReviewTrigger: Revision of creamy layer income threshold by DoPT.
Changes to the Central List of OBCs by NCBC recommendation.
State-level changes to the OBC certificate application process.
Introduction of new digital application platforms or unified national portal.
